findings.message: The two new choices added to fix the engine-trace single-choice error (story.r8.json lines 373-385, choices "trace-on" and "call-out") both target "nib" with no requires/effects difference between them. They are not a genuine branch point: whichever label the reader picks, the next passage, state, items and clues are identical. This clears the automated graph check but not the underlying problem it was flagging (give the reader a real decision), and it does not match the stated intent of revision 8 ("connector passages fixed, zero single-choice" implying real branching, not a cosmetic duplicate).

Same defect in the nib-ask connector (story.r8.json lines 423-435, choices "nib-ask-on" and "promise-nib"): both target "threshold" with no state difference. The "promise-nib" label ("Promise Nib you will be careful, then go to the door") implies a consequence, but no flag, item, clue or later passage ever reflects the promise - it is cosmetic filler added only to satisfy the single-choice validator, not a real decision.

By contrast, the other two passages revision 8 was meant to fix are genuine fixes: hull-marks (lines 164-186) now forks to "tube" vs "locker" (a real shortcut that changes which passages are read and whether hook-pole is picked up on that path), and porthole (lines ~243-262) forks to "inside" vs "dome" (skips the quiet-corridor passage). These two are fine and should be the model for fixing engine-trace and nib-ask the same way, e.g. by giving one option a distinct destination or a distinct item/clue/flag effect.
